_about: Where each kind of usable belonging goes on a 'group' step. The goal is a home per kind of thing (a labeled box, a drawer, a hook, a room), so areas condense over time and anything found later has somewhere to go. Entries are matched in order against item labels, so put specific kinds before general ones (e.g. 'pet supplies' before 'dishes' so a dog bowl doesn't go to the sink). 'keywords' match whole words (plurals ending in s/es included; list irregular plurals like 'knives' separately). 'home' is the real place it lives. 'fallback' is a concrete stand-in for when that home doesn't exist yet: prefer a container they likely have (a shoebox, a sturdy box, a bin) over 'a pile'; a laundry basket is only for laundry, never dishes or toys. 'box_label' is what to write on the box with a marker; null when the home is a room, a hook, or a spot rather than a box. 'tip' is one small, practical way to put this kind of thing away; null when there's nothing useful to add. 'rooms' (optional) overrides any of these fields by the room the photo shows (living_room, bedroom, kitchen, dining_room, bathroom, office, entryway, laundry_room, garage, closet); the entry's own fields are for any other room or when the room isn't clear.

homes.home: back on the couch, chair, or bed they belong to
homes.fallback: stacked at one end of the couch or bed
homes.tip: Fluff each one and stand it up against the back; it takes seconds and makes the whole seat look reset.

living_room.home: back on the couch or chairs
living_room.fallback: stacked at one end of the couch

bedroom.home: back on the bed, or on the closet shelf
bedroom.fallback: stacked at the head of the bed

homes.home: stuffed inside one bag, kept under the kitchen sink
homes.fallback: all stuffed inside one bag, hung on a doorknob
homes.tip: Push them all into one bag loosely; no folding needed.

homes.home: one box labeled 'Keepsakes', kept somewhere dry
homes.fallback: a shoebox or bag set aside just for keepsakes
homes.tip: No need to look through them today; just lay them in flat so nothing bends.

homes.home: one bag or bin labeled 'Gift wrap'
homes.fallback: one gift bag holding all the others
homes.tip: Stand rolls upright in the bin so they don't crush.

homes.home: one bin labeled with the holiday, stored up high or in a closet
homes.fallback: a box or bag just for decorations
homes.tip: Wrap string lights loosely around your hand or a piece of cardboard so they don't tangle.

homes.home: one bin labeled 'Pet', near where the pet eats
homes.fallback: a grocery bag set by the pet's bowl
homes.tip: Leashes can hang on a hook by the door so they're easy to grab.

homes.home: a windowsill or table with some light
homes.fallback: together on one tray or plate near a window
homes.tip: A plate or tray under each pot keeps water off the floor.

homes.home: under the kitchen or bathroom sink
homes.fallback: one bucket or bag, standing upright
homes.tip: Keep sprays and bottles standing up with caps closed, away from food.

homes.home: one bowl or tray by the door
homes.fallback: a small cup or bowl by the door
homes.tip: One landing spot means you'll always know where to look.

homes.home: a small dish, tray, or box on the dresser
homes.fallback: a mug or small bowl on the dresser
homes.tip: Clasp necklaces before setting them down so they don't knot.

homes.home: a hook or the coat closet by the door
homes.fallback: draped over one chair by the door
homes.tip: Hats, scarves, and gloves can share one basket on the closet floor.

bedroom.fallback: draped over one chair or the end of the bed

homes.home: hung together on the closet rod
homes.fallback: one stack on the closet floor
homes.tip: Hook them all facing the same way so they come off one at a time.

homes.home: a drawer or box just for cables
homes.fallback: a shoebox or grocery bag just for cables
homes.tip: Loosely loop each one and tuck the end through, or use a twist tie from the kitchen; no need to match them to devices today.

homes.home: one small box labeled 'Batteries & bulbs'
homes.fallback: a zip bag or small container
homes.tip: Put a bit of tape over the ends of 9-volt batteries so they can't touch metal.

homes.home: a shelf or box just for electronics
homes.fallback: a shoebox or bag for electronics, kept off the floor
homes.tip: Lay them in flat with screens facing each other, not stacked loose on top.

homes.home: the kitchen, next to the sink
homes.fallback: stacked on a tray or in a sturdy box by the doorway, ready to carry to the kitchen in one trip
homes.tip: Stack plates with plates and cups with cups; put knives in point-down or lay them flat on top.

homes.home: the kitchen cupboard or pantry
homes.fallback: a grocery bag by the doorway, ready to carry to the kitchen
homes.tip: Sealed food only; anything opened or past its date can go in the trash bag instead.

homes.home: a shoe rack or one row by the door
homes.fallback: one row along the wall by the door, pairs side by side
homes.tip: Pair them up as you go; a single without its partner can wait at the end of the row.

bedroom.home: one row on the closet floor
bedroom.fallback: one row along the wall by the closet, pairs side by side

homes.home: along the edge of the room, against the wall and out of the walkway
homes.fallback: pushed against the nearest wall, stacked no more than waist high
homes.tip: Heaviest on the bottom, and keep doorways and the path through the room clear.

homes.home: the laundry basket or hamper
homes.fallback: a big bag or pillowcase used as a laundry bag for now
homes.tip: No need to sort clean from dirty today; it all goes in, and washing sorts it.

homes.home: a hook by the door, or nested inside one bag
homes.fallback: one bag holding the others
homes.tip: Empty pockets into a bowl first, then nest the bags; a suitcase can hold the rest.

homes.home: a bookshelf, or a box labeled 'Books'
homes.fallback: one neat stack against the wall, spines facing out
homes.tip: Spines facing out so you can read titles later without unstacking.

homes.home: one tray or box labeled 'Papers', to look through another day
homes.fallback: a shoebox or bag for papers, no reading needed today
homes.tip: Just drop them in facing the same way; sorting is a separate step for another day.

homes.home: folded on the bed or in the linen closet
homes.fallback: folded in half and stacked at the foot of the bed
homes.tip: A rough fold in half, then half again, is plenty.

living_room.home: folded over the back or arm of the couch
living_room.fallback: folded and stacked at one end of the couch

bedroom.home: folded on the bed, or on the closet shelf
bedroom.fallback: folded in half and stacked at the foot of the bed

homes.home: one bin labeled 'Medicine', up high and out of reach of kids and pets
homes.fallback: a zip bag or container on a high shelf
homes.tip: Keep everything in its original bottle so the labels stay with it.

homes.home: the bathroom, or a bin labeled 'Bathroom'
homes.fallback: a basket or bag by the doorway, ready to carry to the bathroom
homes.tip: Stand bottles upright with caps closed; hot tools go in only once they're cool.

homes.home: a cup or small box on the desk
homes.fallback: a mug on the desk
homes.tip: Pens and pencils point-down in a cup; small bits like clips in a separate dish.

homes.home: a box labeled 'Tools'
homes.fallback: a sturdy bag or bucket just for tools
homes.tip: Loose screws and nails can go in a jar or zip bag inside the box.

homes.home: one bin or corner for sports gear
homes.fallback: a box or bin in one corner
homes.tip: Balls in the bin, long things like bats standing in a corner.

homes.home: a box labeled with the hobby, like 'Crafts'
homes.fallback: a tote or bag just for craft supplies
homes.tip: Close paint and glue lids first; small bits can go in a zip bag inside the box.

homes.home: a shelf or box labeled 'Games & movies'
homes.fallback: one stack on a shelf or against the wall
homes.tip: Loose discs back in any case for now, even if it's the wrong one.

homes.home: a bin or box labeled 'Toys'
homes.fallback: any box or bin just for toys
homes.tip: Small pieces like Lego can go in a zip bag so they don't scatter.

homes.home: a shelf or tabletop, or leaning against the wall
homes.fallback: together on one shelf or clear spot of table
homes.tip: Frames and mirrors lean face-in against the wall so the glass is protected.

default.home: a box labeled with what's inside
default.fallback: a bag or box for now, with anything similar
